newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds prove more restrained.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds prove more restrained.

text.p: *Australian bonds put in a much restrained performance after last week's sell-off, although price moves to the upside proved short-lived ahead of upcoming reports on wages.
Australian bonds put in a much more restrained performance after last week's aggressive sell-off, although price moves to the upside proved short-lived ahead of upcoming reports on wages.

Concerns over wages outcomes have been put back at the top of the agenda following last week's Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Bulletin, but any other signs of unexpected strength within the economy will also prove detrimental, analysts said.
Long dated bond yields jumped some 25 basis points last week after data showed that fourth quarter growth may not have been as soft as anticipated.

Economists surveyed by Reuters last Friday gave a preliminary median forecast for fourth quarter GDP of 0.5 percent growth compared with 0.3 percent earlier this month after last week's jump in company profits.
The full GDP release is due on March 4.
A further GDP component, capital expenditure, is due for release on Thursday, but eyes will be firmly on the final average weekly ordinary time earnings due at the same time.
The latest report enterprise bargianing agreements by the Department of Industrial Relations is also expected to emerge on Wednesday.
Last week's rise in yields could well be the sign of things to come over the remainder of the year.
"We clearly think that the interest rate cycle has bottomed," said Jeff Oughton, senior economist at NAB.

"As rates in the U.S. rise modestly over the next year and as some wages and inflation pressures emerge towards the end of the year here, 10-year bonds will be back towards 7-3/4, 8.0 percent," he added.
Local bonds, and debt markets globally, are also cautiously awaiting Federal Reserve Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday and Thursday.

Bond yield spreads to the dollar bloc crept out slightly during the course of the day. U.S. Treasury yields showed little change in Tokyo after ending marginally lower in New York on Friday. New Zealand debt outperformed, supported by a firm N.Z. dollar ahead of Tuesday's quarterly employment survey.
